transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what’s been bringing you in today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you for seeing me. I really hope I'm not taking up time from someone who needs it more. 

Um... my wife is actually the one who wanted me to come in. She got pretty scared about... well, I guess I've been noticing some weird things lately. It's probably nothing, just stress or my mind playing tricks on me, right? But I keep hearing water running... and, um... this is a little embarrassing to admit because I really don't want you to think badly of me, but I've been hearing men whispering inside the walls when nobody else is in the house. 

And sometimes I'll see this dark, wet patch spreading across the hallway floor. I always go over and check it, and it's completely dry. I keep telling her it's just the plumbing or shadows, but it really frightened her. That's... that's an okay reason to be here, right?
Can you describe more about the whispers you hear inside the walls? Are they voices you recognize, or do they say specific things that concern you?

Um... no, I don't recognize the voices at all. I hope that doesn't make me sound too crazy. It's mostly just... like a low murmuring. Like a couple of guys having a conversation just behind the drywall. I can't ever quite make out the specific words they're saying. Which is probably a good thing, right? I really don't want to make it sound worse than it actually is. 

Like I was saying a second ago, I think what finally scared my wife so much wasn't just the whispering, but that it happens when I hear the water running... and then I'll see that dark wet patch spreading across the hallway. I'll go right over and feel it, and it's completely dry. I know it doesn't make any sense, and I try not to bother her with it, but she noticed me checking the floor and got really worried. 

I'm sorry, I feel like I'm just repeating myself now. Am I giving you the right kind of information? I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions properly.
Do these experiences with the whispers and the wet patch happen in a certain pattern or situation, like at specific times of day or when you're feeling a particular way?

Um... a pattern. Well, I guess... I hope it's okay to explain it like this. It wasn't always happening, I promise. Before all these house problems dragged on and on, and I kind of... well, fell into this depression... I never experienced any of this. 

I never used to hear voices in the walls or see those wet patches that weren't really there. All of that... it really only showed up after I had already stopped caring about my usual life. I was just waking up every day feeling like a complete failure, and then these weird things started happening. 

And... um... I really hate to admit this next part, because I don't want you to think I'm completely losing my mind, but... it was around that same time I started thinking the neighbors were tracking me, too. Which I know sounds terrible! I know it does, and I'm so embarrassed to even say it out loud. But none of that happened before I got so down on myself and stopped functioning normally. 

Does... does that make sense? I hope that answers your question about the timing of it all. I'm really trying to give you what you need.
Have you ever experienced a period of time where you felt unusually energized, needed less sleep, or had racing thoughts, even if it seemed like a good thing at the time?

Um... unusually energized? No, I... I don't think so. I mean, I definitely haven't felt anything like that lately, that's for sure. 

I've never really been the type to have tons of energy or need less sleep. If anything, I usually feel like I need more sleep than I actually get, especially lately with... well, everything. And racing thoughts? I don't think I've ever had that. My thoughts are usually pretty slow and heavy, to be honest. 

I hope that's an okay answer. I just... I want to be completely honest with you, and I really can't remember a time where I felt super energized or like my mind was going a mile a minute in a good way. Is it okay that I haven't experienced that? I just want to make sure I'm not missing something important that you need to know.
Have you ever had beliefs or ideas that other people around you didn’t share, even though you were sure they were true at the time?

Um... beliefs that other people didn't share? I guess... well, I know I mentioned the neighbors earlier. And I really, really hope this doesn't make me sound completely irrational. I know how it sounds to other people, I really do. 

But... um... with the house, and all the problems we had with it... I started feeling absolutely certain that the mold and the bad wiring... that it had somehow poisoned everything I own. Like, everything I touched was contaminated by it. My wife tried to tell me it was impossible, and I know she was just trying to help, but I just... I couldn't shake the feeling that it was true. 

And then... well, I started thinking that the neighbors knew about it, too. Like they were watching me, just waiting to see when I would mess up again, or when the poison would finally get to me. 

I know it sounds so far-fetched when I say it out loud to a doctor. I'm sorry, I really don't want you to think I'm completely disconnected from reality. I just... at the time, it felt so real to me. Is it okay that I'm telling you this? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of examples for what you're asking.
Have you ever had a strong belief that something was true, even when others showed you evidence that it wasn’t, and you still couldn’t let go of that belief?

Um... well, yes, I suppose that's exactly what I was just trying to explain... I hope I didn't confuse things by bringing it up too early. 

It's just like I said about the house. My wife kept trying to show me that things were fine, you know? She'd wipe down the counters or point out that the air was clear, but... I just couldn't let it go. I'm still certain that the mold and that awful wiring have somehow poisoned everything I own. I know she thinks I'm being stubborn, and I know it sounds so far-fetched to say it out loud... but I just feel it so strongly. 

And the neighbors... my wife says they don't even look our way, but I can just tell they're watching me. Like they're just waiting to see when I'm going to mess up again. 

I'm really sorry to repeat myself, I just... I want to make sure I'm answering your question properly. Is that the kind of thing you meant? I promise I'm not trying to be difficult or ignore evidence on purpose, it's just... it just feels so undeniably true to me. I hope you can understand that.
Can you tell me more about your belief that the house has poisoned your belongings? Have you ever acted on this belief, like throwing things away or avoiding parts of the house?

Um... well, I really don't want you to think I'm completely losing my mind, or that I'm, you know, acting out in some crazy way. I try very hard to be reasonable about it. 

But... yes, I guess I have acted on it a little bit. It's just... when you're so absolutely sure that everything is contaminated by that mold and the bad wiring... it's hard to just go about your day normally. I know it sounds far-fetched, I really do. But I'm just so certain it's poisoned everything I own. 

So... um... I have thrown a few things away. Just small things, mostly. Things I couldn't bear to touch anymore because I just knew the poison was on them. And I do try to avoid certain parts of the house when I can, just to be safe. My wife gets a little frustrated with me, and I hate upsetting her, but I just... I can't help it. 

And then there's the neighbors... I try to stay away from the windows because I can just tell they're watching me, waiting to see when the poison gets to me or when I mess up again. 

I'm sorry, I know that probably sounds terrible. I hope I'm not coming across as completely unhinged. I just want to be honest with you about how strong this feeling is. Is it okay that I've been doing these things? I just... I want to make sure I'm doing the right thing by telling you.

Can you tell me more about how you reacted when your wife tried to show you that the house was safe? Did you ever feel like her reassurance was pointless, or that she just didn’t understand the danger?

Um... well... I hope it didn't sound like I was ignoring her on purpose, or that I don't appreciate her trying to help. She really is wonderful, and I know she just wants me to feel better. I don't want you to think I'm ungrateful or... or a bad husband.

But when she would try to reassure me... wiping things down or telling me it was safe... I just... it's hard to explain without sounding completely irrational. I know it sounds far-fetched, I really do. But I'm just so certain the mold and the wiring in that house have poisoned everything I own. It’s not that I think her reassurance is pointless, it’s just... she can't see it the way I do. She doesn't understand that the contamination is already there. 

And it makes me so anxious, especially because... well, like I mentioned, I can tell the neighbors are watching to see when I mess up again, or when it all finally catches up to me. So when she tells me it's fine, I just feel this heavy dread because I know it's not, and I know people are watching. 

I'm sorry, I know I keep bringing up the same things. I just want to make sure I'm explaining it right so you don't think I'm just being stubborn with her. Does that make sense? I hope I'm giving you the kind of answers you need.
When your wife showed you clear proof that something wasn't contaminated or dangerous, did you still feel deep down that it was unsafe, no matter what she showed you?

Um... yes. I really hate to admit it, because it makes me sound so... ungrateful for her help, or like I'm just being difficult on purpose. But yes. Even when she would show me clear proof, like... wiping a surface and showing me the paper towel is clean... deep down, I still felt it was completely unsafe. 

I know I keep repeating myself, and I really apologize for sounding like a broken record today... but no matter what she shows me, I just can't shake it. I'm still absolutely certain that the mold and the bad wiring have poisoned everything I own. It just... it feels like it's seeped into everything, beyond what a paper towel can show, you know? 

And... well, it doesn't help that I can still tell the neighbors are watching me. They're always just waiting to see when I mess up again, or when the contamination finally takes its toll. If things were really fine, they wouldn't be keeping tabs on me like that. 

I try so hard to just smile and agree with my wife so I don't cause any more stress for her, but... inside, I just know it's not safe. I hope that doesn't make me sound too stubborn or unreasonable to you. Am I explaining this okay for your notes? I really just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.

I know I keep repeating myself, and I really apologize for sounding like a broken record today... but no matter what she shows me, I just can't shake it. I'm still absolutely certain that the mold and the bad wiring have poisoned everything I own. It just... it feels like it's seeped into everything, beyond what a paper towel can show, you know? 

And... well, it doesn't help that I can still tell the neighbors are watching me. They're always just waiting to see when I mess up again, or when the contamination finally takes its toll. If things were really fine, they wouldn't be keeping tabs on me like that. 

I try so hard to just smile and agree with my wife so I don't cause any more stress for her, but... inside, I just know it's not safe. I hope that doesn't make me sound too stubborn or unreasonable to you. Am I explaining this okay for your notes? I really just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
